brief.subject: IRS waives dyed diesel penalties; Chicago head tax fight
brief.headline: IRS Explains Dyed Diesel Penalty Relief as Year-End Tax Prep Begins
brief.dek: New IRS FAQs on dyed diesel relief, five IRS year-end steps, Chicago's head tax standoff and California's wealth tax vote.
brief.lede: The IRS has posted FAQs on its suspension of federal tax penalties for highway use of dyed diesel fuel, which runs through the rest of this year.

sections.heading: Dyed Diesel Penalties on Hold
bullets: Federal tax penalties are suspended through the rest of this year when dyed diesel is sold for or used on U.S. highways.
The IRS posted new FAQs this week explaining how the relief works.
Fleet, construction and farm operators should review the FAQs to confirm their fuel use qualifies.

sections.heading: IRS Flags Five Year-End Moves
bullets: The IRS is urging taxpayers to complete five tasks before the end of 2026.
Acting now aims to smooth the coming filing season and head off surprises in April.
The IRS Advisory Council will also hold a public meeting, a chance to track agency priorities.

sections.heading: Chicago Head Tax Faces Pushback
bullets: Mayor Brandon Johnson has again proposed a per-employee corporate tax in his latest city budget pitch.
Gov. JB Pritzker repeated his opposition on Thursday.
Chicago employers should watch the budget talks, since a per-head levy would add a direct cost to hiring.

sections.heading: Big Money Targets California Wealth Tax
bullets: A billionaire-backed group spent more than $50 million over the past week to defeat Proposition 40.
Prop. 40 is a California wealth tax heading into the final stretch before the vote.
